articles.title: Dependency Cooldowns: Make Your Package Manager Wait Before It Trusts New Code
articles.excerpt: Most npm supply-chain attacks follow the same script. Someone phishes a maintainer or steals a publish token, pushes a poisoned patch release, and then waits for every ^1.2.3 range on the planet to pi…
articles.body: Most npm supply-chain attacks follow the same script. Someone phishes a maintainer or steals a publish token, pushes a poisoned patch release, and then waits for every ^1.2.3 range on the planet to pick it up on the next install. The malicious version usually gets spotted and pulled within hours. The damage is done in those hours, by machines that installed it before anyone noticed. A dependency cooldown attacks that window directly. Instead of installing whatever was published thirty seconds ago, your package manager only accepts versions that have existed for a while. It's a boring idea, and that's why it works: you let the rest of the ecosystem be the canary. Every major package manager now supports it, but each one picked its own config key and, annoyingly, its own unit of time.
articles.author: Danny Holloran

articles.title: Our admin panel answers 404 to every signed-in account that is not on a hardcoded list
articles.excerpt: Nakodo has an operator panel at /admin: six pages that read the whole service. Accounts, plans, campaign counts, support threads, inbound mail, the background run log. It is the one surface in the pro…
articles.body: Nakodo has an operator panel at /admin : six pages that read the whole service. Accounts, plans, campaign counts, support threads, inbound mail, the background run log. It is the one surface in the product that can see other people's data, which is exactly the data the privacy notice promises to keep to a short list of uses. So the interesting question is not what the panel shows. It is how it decides who you are, and what it does when the answer is no. Admin is a constant, not a column export const ADMIN_EMAILS : readonly string [] = [ OPERATOR_EMAIL ]; export function isAdminEmail ( email : string | null | undefined ): boolean { return !! email && ADMIN_EMAILS . includes ( email . trim (). toLowerCase ()); } No is_admin column. No ADMIN_EMAILS environment variable.

articles.title: CMMC 2.0 for Defense Contractors: Understanding the Security Boundaries
articles.excerpt: For organizations working in the U.S. defense supply chain, CMMC 2.0 raises a practical technical question: which systems, users, and services are subject to the applicable cybersecurity requirements?…
articles.body: For organizations working in the U.S. defense supply chain, CMMC 2.0 raises a practical technical question: which systems, users, and services are subject to the applicable cybersecurity requirements? The answer begins with the contract and the information being handled. Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) have different protection requirements. CMMC 2.0 uses three levels to align cybersecurity expectations with the sensitivity of that information. The CMMC certification framework outlines the model that defense contractors need to understand when determining their applicable obligations. Level 1: Fundamental Safeguards for FCI Level 1 focuses on basic safeguarding practices associated with FAR 52.204-21.
articles.author: Chethna

articles.title: How I Turned a Complex Fintech Whitepaper Into a Simple Reading Checklist
articles.excerpt: Reading technical documents can become overwhelming quickly. rules; custody; execution; collateral; risk; coordination. This helped me understand why different components exist. I also learned to sepa…
articles.body: Reading technical documents can become overwhelming quickly. My solution was not to learn every term immediately. Instead, I created a simple map: Purpose → Components → Conditions → Questions For Duraqex, I grouped the main concepts by function: rules; custody; execution; collateral; risk; coordination. This helped me understand why different components exist. I also learned to separate two things: what a document describes and what is currently available. That distinction is important in any technical project. A roadmap can describe future capabilities. An architecture document can explain design principles. Neither should automatically be interpreted as the same thing as current user access. My biggest takeaway: good research is not about reading everything.

articles.title: Training Among Us Bots: The Crew That Stopped Fixing the Reactor
articles.excerpt: I train Among Us bots by self-play: the crew and the impostors are both learners, and they play tens of thousands of games against each other and against saved copies of their earlier selves. I run th…
articles.body: I train Among Us bots by self-play: the crew and the impostors are both learners, and they play tens of thousands of games against each other and against saved copies of their earlier selves. I run the training in leagues, each one a roughly ten-hour run that starts from the bots the previous league ended with. The fifth league looked healthy for ten thousand games and then fell over. Between game 10,000 and game 12,500, the impostors' win rate in their own training games went from 50% to 75%, the crew's tasks went from 70% done to 41%, and the impostors almost stopped killing (6.52 kills a game down to 2.00). They had found something better than killing: sabotaging the reactor. The run went on for another 52,500 games and never recovered.

articles.title: What Will the Next Bitcoin Block Look Like?
articles.excerpt: What Will the Next Bitcoin Block Look Like?### A visual way to understand Bitcoin’s transaction queue, fee pressure and next-block estimate When you send Bitcoin, the transaction does not immediately…
articles.body: What Will the Next Bitcoin Block Look Like?### A visual way to understand Bitcoin’s transaction queue, fee pressure and next-block estimate When you send Bitcoin, the transaction does not immediately become part of the blockchain. It first enters the mempool: the changing collection of valid, unconfirmed transactions waiting to be selected by miners. That queue is public, but it is not always easy to read. A block explorer can show individual transactions and fee rates, yet it rarely provides a clear answer to the questions most people actually have: How busy is Bitcoin right now? How much data is waiting? Which transactions may fit into the next block? Where is the current fee cutoff? Is the backlog growing or shrinking?

articles.title: Our structured data is two script tags, and the rule is that no node may claim more than the page shows
articles.excerpt: Every public page on Nakodo ships exactly two blocks of structured data. One comes from the marketing layout and describes the things that exist once: the organisation and the website. One comes from…
articles.body: Every public page on Nakodo ships exactly two blocks of structured data. One comes from the marketing layout and describes the things that exist once: the organisation and the website. One comes from the page and describes what that page actually is. You can read both on any page. View source on a vetting guide and the page block is BreadcrumbList , Article , FAQPage and HowTo . Do the same on the pricing page and it is BreadcrumbList and a SoftwareApplication with three Offer nodes. The rule behind all of it is one sentence, which sits as a comment at the top of the builder file: every node describes something the page shows a reader. Markup that claims more than the page does is a manual action waiting to happen, not a ranking trick.

articles.body: TL;DR Several major Google services on Googlebook, including Gmail, Docs, Calendar, Sheets, and YouTube, run as web-based experiences rather than native Android apps. Google says this is intentional because it considers the desktop web versions of some apps the better laptop experience. The tradeoff becomes more noticeable on touchscreen and convertible Googlebooks, where native Android apps can be easier to use in tablet mode. One of the biggest Googlebook attractions sounds wonderfully straightforward: take Android, stretch it into a proper desktop operating system, and bring the enormous Play Store library along for the ride. Google has leaned heavily on that app story, even adding labels that tell you which Android apps are best suited to a desktop.

articles.title: A faint glow from the early universe could help solve the mystery of dark energy
articles.excerpt: Hydrogen may be the most common element in the cosmos, but scientists could use it to do something unique: uncover the nature of dark energy.
articles.body: Hydrogen may be the most common element in the cosmos, but scientists could use it to do something unique: uncover the nature of dark energy, the mysterious force driving the accelerating expansion of the universe. This new line of dark energy investigation comes from the fact that researchers have determined that the CHIME (Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) project can detect the faint radio glow of hydrogen from the universe's distant past. Not only does this represent a faster and much less expensive way to investigate dark energy, but it is a major milestone for CHIME. The instrument was specifically devised to investigate dark energy and its pervasive influence.

articles.body: Over the course of 218 episodes spanning 11 seasons, the landmark TV series The X-Files explored a wide array of science fiction concepts, including a few episodes that touched on the idea of time travel. There was the season 4 episode “Synchrony,” where an elderly time traveler goes back to the 1990s to stop his younger self from inventing time travel. Then there’s the Groundhog Day -like season 6 episode “Monday,” which sees Agent Mulder (David Duchovny) and Agent Scully (Gillian Anderson) repeatedly trying to stop a bank bombing while experiencing the same day over and over again. articles.body: SpaceX just broke an uncharacteristically long Starlink launch drought. The company sent 27 of its Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) today (Oct. 12), launching them atop a Falcon 9 rocket from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:28 p.m. EDT (5:28 p.m. local time; 0028 GMT on Oct. 13) It was the first Starlink mission for a Falcon 9 since Sept. 19 , which was another 27-satellite liftoff from Vandenberg. For some perspective on this recent gap: Between Aug. 19 and Sept. 6, a span of 19 days, SpaceX launched seven Starlink missions with Falcon 9s. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a ship at sea shortly after the Oct. 12 launch. articles.title: Astronomers witness supermassive black hole gorge on a cosmic meal before 'burping' radio jets 300 days later
articles.excerpt: Using the NASA spacecraft Swift, astronomers observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal.
articles.body: Using the NASA X-ray spacecraft Swift combined with radio observations, astronomers have observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal. The team was also able to roughly estimate the mass of this feeding cosmic titan, which sits at the heart of the Perseus Cluster, a massive collection of thousands of galaxies. The black hole sits at the center of the galaxy NGC 1275, located around 225 light-years away, and is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus Cluster . The supermassive black hole first flared in X-rays, which indicated an increase in the rate at which it was accreting matter.

articles.title: The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.
articles.body: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions. The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here . NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits.

articles.body: Friday, October 16, 2026 Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses.
